title: Hess Midstream upgraded at Raymond James as Chevron restructuring selloff overdone - TradingView
content: Hess Midstream HESM rose 2.2% in Friday's trading as Raymond James raised its rating to Market Outperform from Market Perform with a $32 price target, saying its recent selloff following the Chevron CVX restructuring has created an attractive entry point for investors. The Bakken contract reset was severe, reducing estimated 2027 EBITDA by $400M while pausing distribution growth and increasing leverage, yet Chevron's CVX ~38% ownership cancellation, contribution of D-J Basin assets, and contract extensions to 2045 provide Hess Midstream HESM with a meaningful exchange of value for the lower rates, Raymond James analyst J.R. Weston said. The pause in 2027 distribution growth has weighted on Hess Midstream HESM sentiment, but the payout looks supported by $525M-$625M of guided adjusted free cash flow against $420M-$425M of distribution, which Weston said should allow leverage to move from 3.75x-4x to the 3.5x-3.75x longer-term target through 2029. While fixed reservation payments expire after 2029, the analyst expects the existing payout to remain covered via retained free cash flow, modest D-J growth, and potential operating efficiencies. title: Chevron vs. ExxonMobil: Which Stock Has the Edge at 52-Week Highs? - TradingView
content: Energy giants Chevron Corporation CVX and ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM are attracting investor attention as their shares approach 52-week highs. CVX trades at $226.68, near its 52-week high of $229.04, while XOM changes hands at $178.23 against a high of $180.31. Rising crude prices have supported the stock’s recent gains, with Brent crude surging above $110 per barrel. Both companies benefit from oil and gas production, refining operations and disciplined capital allocation. However, buying near yearly peaks calls for examining whether operational improvements justify continued optimism. Their respective exposure to Guyana, the Permian Basin and downstream markets offers a common basis for comparing production growth, cash generation, operating efficiency and shareholder rewards. Chevron’s appeal centers on its enlarged upstream portfolio following the Hess acquisition. Second-quarter 2026 worldwide production reached 4.07 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, rising 20% year over year, aided by legacy Hess assets and growth in the Permian Basin and Gulf of America. Management expects full-year output of 3.98 million to 4.10 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Its Guyana exposure also provides high-margin oil growth opportunities into the next decade. Cost discipline is another advantage. CVX achieved $1.5 billion in annualized Hess-related synergies, exceeding its original goal, while securing $3 billion in annual structural savings since 2024. These efforts can protect margins when commodity prices retreat. The company also expects to spend 25% less capital per barrel of oil equivalent in its U.S. shale and tight operations this year than last year, indicating stronger capital productivity. Chevron’s financial flexibility supports its investment appeal. It generated $22.6 billion in operating cash flow and $18.1 billion in free cash flow during the second quarter, while reducing total debt by $8.4 billion. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. title: 3 Energy Dividend Stocks to Buy for More Than Oil Exposure - The Globe and Mail
content: Energy stocks can appeal to investors who want regular income, especially when markets are unsettled. Attacks on Saudi energy facilities and threats to tankers in the Middle East have increased uncertainty about oil supplies, giving investors another reason to look closely at how companies earn cash and pay dividends. ChevronCVX, Canadian Natural ResourcesCNQ and Kinder Morgan KMI,  are three dividend-paying energy stocks to buy. Their favorable ranks support the selection, while regular payouts add an income component to the investment case. Brent crude is around $110 a barrel, while U.S. crude is near $100. Attacks on Saudi energy facilities and ships near the Strait of Hormuz have raised fears of supply disruptions. Even if production continues, concerns that oil may not reach buyers can keep prices high. Saudi oil exports have nevertheless recovered. They reached a five-month high in August despite lower production. Later shipping estimates suggested crude exports were nearing pre-war levels. Delivering fuel remains a challenge. Restrictions on refined-fuel shipments and high shipping costs can squeeze refiners’ profits and raise costs for consumers. U.S. crude stockpiles also fell more than expected, adding to concerns about available supplies. Higher crude prices can help oil producers earn more, but they do not benefit every energy business equally. Expensive shipping and feedstock can raise costs elsewhere in the industry. That makes company cash flow a more useful starting point than a broad bet on oil. For dividend investors, the question is whether a company can cover its payout after funding its operations and necessary investment. Borrowing to maintain distributions would offer less comfort than paying them from cash the business generates. Kinder Morgan, Chevron and Canadian Natural Resources give investors different ways to approach energy income. Their ability to fund dividends after covering operating costs and investment needs matters most. Steady cash generation can help support those payments when energy prices weaken. Oil prices could stay high if attacks continue or shipping faces more disruptions. A recovery in exports or easing of the conflict could bring prices down. With both outcomes possible, investors should avoid relying on a single oil-price forecast. Established dividend payers can offer a more balanced approach. Their size, financial resources and ability to generate cash from different operations can help them navigate commodity-market swings while continuing to return capital to investors. Against this backdrop, Kinder Morgan, Chevron and Canadian Natural Resources offer three different ways to participate in the energy market while maintaining an income focus. MRNA stock closed 1.54% higher after TD Cowen raised its price target. CVX stock ended the session 0.45% up amid rising oil prices and a price target hike from Bank of America. V stock was 0.31% higher at close after announcing three new capabilities across its commercial card growth, virtual card security and agentic commerce for commercial payments. MRNA stock climbed to an annual high of $254.48 on Wednesday, marking three consecutive sessions in the green ahead of its third-quarter results expected on Nov. 6. TD Cowen raised the price target on Moderna and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares. The firm said that it had updated its model ahead of Q3 results and increased the estimate for peak INT profit to Moderna to roughly $3.4 billion in 2035 versus its prior $830 million to reflect its potential commercial opportunities in adjuvant melanoma and NSCLC drugs. Earlier in the week, BofA raised the price target to $220 from $200 and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares. The firm said that with topline success of INTerpath-001 already confirmed, the focus at ESMO will be on the magnitude of benefit of the combo as read-across to upcoming readouts in RCC and MIBC, adding that it expects the presentation to be "a positive data point." The firm noted that U.S. refiners are benefiting from expensive crude shipping, and that CDU growth is expected in the fourth quarter, though that material growth is not enough to offset the 2+ mmbpd offline in Russia and 2.5 mmbpd reduction in the Middle East. (IBM) stock is heading for its best week since June after the company’s fiscal third-quarter (Q3) 2026 results highlighted strong software growth and infrastructure demand. CEO Arvind Krishna said Q2 weakness “reflected timing rather than underlying demand,” while distributed infrastructure surged 32%, providing optimism about mainframe momentum and enterprise AI spending. International Business Machines stock traded over 4% lower overnight, reversing nearly 4% gains in the regular session. IBM’s software division grew 9% in Q3, while infrastructure revenue rose 5%. Consulting also showed a modest improvement of 2%, Krishna said during the company’s Q3 earnings call. “Transaction processing grew 10%, underscoring the strategic importance of the mainframe and validating our view that the softness we saw in the second quarter reflected timing rather than underlying demand.” IBM’s distributed infrastructure business grew 32% in Q3, boosting overall infrastructure revenue. Its latest Z17 mainframe platform also performed well. “Z17 continued the strongest innovation cycle in the platform's history, generating more than $1 billion of incremental revenue over 6 quarters compared with prior programs. This reflects the security, reliability, scalability and compelling economics of the platform. As infrastructure costs rise, IBM Z delivers a 2 to 15x total cost of ownership advantage versus off-platform alternatives.” Krishna contended that businesses need good data, secure systems and flexible cloud services to make AI useful. He vouched for IBM real-time data tools offering AI-powered software development, task automation, cost control, and cloud computing to help companies use AI across their operations. On July 14, IBM shares fell more than 25% in a day, marking their biggest single-day drop in over 50 years. The sell-off followed a surprise update ahead of its Q2 earnings, in which Krishna said results were “worse than our expectations.” IBM reported preliminary revenue of $17.2 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.93 per share, missing Street estimates. The disappointing update raised concerns across the enterprise technology sector. The rout came as companies unexpectedly shifted IT spending away from IBM’s software and consulting services toward hardware, memory chips, and servers because of AI-driven supply shortages. As a result, IBM’s Infrastructure division revenue fell 7% in Q2. Krishna admitted that the company did not respond quickly enough to rising chip costs and changing customer demand. (TSLA) as earnings season kicks into full throttle this week. As of 10:39 p.m. EDT, Nasdaq-100 futures were down 1%, S&P 500 futures fell 0.49% and Dow futures slipped 0.21%. Meta’s revenue for the third quarter climbed 26% to $64.6 billion, surpassing Wall Street expectations of $63.4 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share of $3.83 missed projections of $5.46 a share due to a $9.89 billion legal charge. The Facebook parent also said its board had approved a new class of non-voting Class C shares to be distributed through a one-time dividend that effectively creates a 2-for-1 split. The company said the fresh stock would help raise capital, structure employee compensation, and fund potential acquisitions amid AI competition. Meanwhile, CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted the success of Meta’s Muse, noting that it has attracted over 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada since its Sept. 8 launch. Zuckerberg said that even as growth remains strong, the company is eyeing a billion users in the next few years. Deepwater Asset Management managing partner Gene Munster noted in a post on X that Zuckerberg’s commentary suggests Muse models and agents will become the center of Meta’s universe. “My take: In three years, Muse will become the lens consumers engage with Instagram, FB, WhatsApp, Reels,” he said. Shares of Lam Research (LRCX) tumbled about 8% to $242 in overnight trading late on Wednesday despite record fiscal first-quarter results, as the chip-equipment maker disclosed supply constraints delaying some shipments and warned that China’s revenue contribution would fall in the December quarter. LRCX stock fell 1% to $260.81 on Wednesday, with shares on pace to log their third straight week of losses after dipping 1% so far this week. Lam reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion, beating the $8.14 billion consensus and setting a fifth consecutive quarterly record. Revenue increased 54% from a year ago and 22% sequentially, while adjusted EPS reached a record $2.20, above the $2.18 estimate. Gross margin improved to 52.4% from 52% in the June quarter. Operating margin climbed to 40.2% from 38.4%, crossing 40% for the first time. Memory systems revenue surged 120% year over year, while NAND revenue grew 40% sequentially. The Customer Support Business Group also delivered strong growth, with revenue rising 40% from a year earlier to nearly $2.5 billion. Lam generated record free cash flow of $3.24 billion and ended the quarter with $7.5 billion in cash and short-term investments, up from $5.6 billion in June. It repurchased $1 billion of shares and paid $325 million in dividends. The company has $3 billion remaining under its overall buyback authorization, with an accelerated repurchase program continuing into December. Its long-term goal remains returning 85% of free cash flow to shareholders. Lam forecast December-quarter revenue of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, and adjusted EPS of $2.33, plus or minus $0.15, versus consensus of $2.32. Gross and operating margins are expected to reach 52.5% and 40.5%, respectively, each plus or minus one percentage point. However, CFO Doug Bettinger said supply constraints limited the outlook. “I would mention that this revenue guide would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints that we are actively managing,” he said. He declined to confirm an analyst’s estimated $300 million to $400 million impact, but said affected December shipments would move into March. CEO Tim Archer said some suppliers face demand growing faster than Lam’s own business. The company is working to expand supplier capacity and would consider investments if needed. “For those of us who were around during the COVID shortages, this is nothing like that. We learned a lot of lessons during that period,” Archer said. “I think we’ll be caught up very shortly.” Lam spent $258 million on capital projects and added about 1,900 employees during Q1. Inventory reached $4.6 billion, while inventory turns improved to a nearly seven-year high. The firm sees longer-term gross margins reaching the mid-50s. However, the adjusted tax rate rose to 16.5% from 11% in June and is expected to remain around that level in December and likely beyond. China accounted for 35% of September revenue, up from 26% in June, but Lam expects the share to fall substantially in December. “I expect that in December we’ll be meaningfully down, driven by the domestic customers in China,” Bettinger said. Multinational customers in China are expected to remain reasonably strong, although Bettinger did not quantify the overall decline. He also expects mature-node spending outside China to strengthen in 2027, with little meaningful growth this year. Lam expects AI demand to sustain semiconductor investment beyond the current supply constraints. “Our preliminary 2027 WFE outlook is for more than $200 billion of spending, with percentage growth led by DRAM, followed by leading-edge foundry logic and NAND,” Archer said. This compares with spending in the mid-$150 billion range expected for 2026. Lam sees demand through 2028 and 10 new major fabs opening in 2027. It also expects calendar 2026 systems revenue to grow well over 40%, marking a third consecutive year of industry outperformance. Foundry logic and DRAM have contributed 80% of systems revenue growth year-to-date. AI’s need for faster storage could further increase equipment demand. “Said differently, for each percentage point mix shift of NAND bits to SLC class devices, approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity will be needed to support the same bit demand,” Archer said. Lam raised its cumulative Aether-related revenue forecast through the decade’s end by $1 billion to $2.5 billion. Advanced packaging is expected to grow about 70% in 2026. “I would be stunned if advanced packaging didn’t grow nicely next year,” Bettinger said. Lam has shipped panel-plating systems to more than 20 customers and secured four backside-power tool-of-record wins at a leading customer. Archer also sees a shift to 3D DRAM increasing demand for Lam’s manufacturing processes. The support business is expected to grow more than 30% in 2026 and more than 15% in 2027, driven by upgrades, spares and services. title: Can ExxonMobil Strengthen Its Long-Term Upstream Production Capacity? - The Globe and Mail
content: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM is well-positioned to expand long-term upstream production capacity, supported by elevated crude oil prices and a strong portfolio of low-cost production assets. Per the U.S. Energy Information Administration's short-term energy outlook, West Texas Intermediate crude prices are projected to average $88.21 per barrel in 2026 and $79.74 in 2027. This favorable pricing environment is expected to support ExxonMobil's cash generation, providing greater financial flexibility to invest in high-return drilling opportunities and expand its oil and gas production. ExxonMobil's upstream production growth strategy centers on its low-cost assets in the Permian Basin and offshore Guyana, where operational efficiencies and technological advancements are strengthening production economics. The company expects its Permian production to grow at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 9% through 2030, reaching nearly 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMBoe/d). Meanwhile, Guyana's offshore resources development remains a key growth driver, with the fifth floating production, storage and offloading (“FPSO”) vessel expected to add 50,000 barrels per day of production capacity following its planned startup in the fourth quarter of 2026. Low production costs and strong crude prices are likely to improve investment returns, encouraging development of these high-quality resources. XOM aims to increase total upstream production to approximately 5.5 MMBoe/d by 2030, with advantaged assets accounting for nearly 65% of total output. The company's focus on capital discipline, structural cost reductions and efficient project execution is expected to strengthen profitability while supporting additional production capacity. Despite commodity price volatility and geopolitical uncertainties, ExxonMobil's low-cost asset base, favorable oil price outlook and expanding project pipeline provide a solid foundation for sustainable upstream production growth. Chevron Corporation CVX and ConocoPhillips COP are pursuing upstream production growth by investing in high-quality resources, supported by a favorable crude oil pricing environment. Chevron's acquisition of Hess, along with rising production from the Permian Basin and Gulf of America, is strengthening its position in key oil-producing regions. In the second quarter of 2026, the energy giant recorded a 20% year-over-year increase in worldwide production. CVX's emphasis on operational efficiency, capital discipline and cost optimization is expected to support additional production growth and improve long-term returns. ConocoPhillips is strengthening its upstream portfolio through investments in the Lower 48 region and major development projects with long-term production potential. The upstream player has agreed to purchase a 42% stake in a joint venture involving oil fields in northern Iraq's Kirkuk region, expanding its access to additional hydrocarbon resources. Chevron has made four executive shifts, including naming a new chief financial officer, according to an announcement from the energy giant earlier this month. The changes will take effect Jan. 1, 2027. Eimear Bonner, currently Chevron's chief financial officer, will become president of oil, products and gas, where she will be responsible for safe, reliable operations across the entire value chain, capital allocation and value chain optimization, per the announcement. Bonner has served in a number of roles with Chevron during her career, including president of the Chevron Technical Center and chief technology officer, according to her biography on the company's website. Jeff Gustavson, who is currently president of new energies, will succeed Bonner as CFO, becoming responsible for audit, controller, investor relations, tax, treasury and business planning activities worldwide. Gustavson joined the company in 1999 and has held multiple roles across several divisions, including finance, M&A, corporate strategic planning, and upstream, according to his bio on the company's website. Mark Nelson, currently vice chairman and executive vice president of oil, products and gas, will be leaving the EVP position, a Chevron spokesperson confirmed. Nelson will remain vice chairman "with responsibility for strategy and business development," and will be responsible for "identifying and advancing opportunities that strengthen the company's portfolio, enhance competitiveness, and support long-term growth," Chevron said in the announcement. In his nearly 40-year career with Chevron, Nelson has held a number of other positions, including executive vice president of strategic business solutions and vice president of midstream, strategy and policy, according to his biography on the company's website. Finally, Brent Gros, president of offshore, will become president of new energies, leading Chevron's lower carbon businesses, like hydrogen, carbon capture and biofuels. He will also oversee the company's AI strategy. "Mark, Eimear, Jeff and Brent bring a combination of operational expertise, strategic perspective and a proven ability to deliver results across our business," said Mike Wirth, Chevron's chairman and CEO.
